l2/geburtsort|place of birth||
l2/wohnort|place of residence||
l2/familienstand|marital status||Singular only. st at the start of "stand" sounds like "sht".
l2/verheiratet|married|Are you married?|
l2/ledig|single, unmarried|I'm single.|A final -ig sounds like "-ikh".
l2/verwitwet|widowed||
l2/alt|old; … years old|My son is ten years old.|
l2/jahr|year; (years of) age|I'm twenty years old.|The h is silent: "yaar". Saying your age: Ich bin zwanzig Jahre alt.
l2/alter|age|Age: nineteen.|
l2/wie-alt|How old are you? (informal)||
l2/wie-alt-sind-sie|How old are you? (polite)||
l2/wo-geboren|Where were you born? (polite)||
l2/haben-sie-kinder|Do you have children?|Yes, I have two children.|
l2/keine-kinder|I don't have any children.||keine = no, not any. Covered in detail in a later lesson.
l2/hauptstadt|capital (city)|Berlin is the capital of Germany.|Haupt- = main + Stadt = city. st in "-stadt" sounds like "sht".
l2/liegen|to lie, to be located|Hanoi is in Vietnam.|Used for places: Hamburg liegt in Deutschland. Plural: Hamburg und Kiel liegen …

l2/sueden|south||

l2/westen|west||

l2/kennen|to know (people, places)|Do you know Berlin?|kennen = to know someone or somewhere; wissen = to know a fact.
l2/also|so, well, that is|So, this is my family.|Careful: also does not mean "also" (that is auch).
l2/arzt|doctor (male)|My father is a doctor.|rzt sounds like "rtst".
l2/aerztin|doctor (female)|My mother is a doctor.|
l2/polizei|police||Singular only. Er ist bei der Polizei = he works for the police.
l2/partner|partner (male)||
l2/partnerin|partner (female)||

l2/koeln|Cologne — big city on the Rhine||
l2/stuttgart|Stuttgart — city in south-west Germany||st at the start of a word sounds like "sht".
l2/kiel|Kiel — port city in northern Germany||
l2/wien|Vienna — capital of Austria||Say "Veen". Don't confuse it with Wein (wine).
l2/salzburg|Salzburg — Austrian city, Mozart's birthplace||
l2/graz|Graz — Austria's second-largest city||
l2/linz|Linz — Austrian city on the Danube||

l3/banane|banana|I'm buying three bananas.|
l3/butter|butter|I need butter.|Singular only. Short u (double t).
l3/ei|egg|I need ten eggs.|Ei sounds like "eye"; the plural Eier sounds like "eye-a".
l3/mehl|flour|Do we have flour?|Singular only. Silent h, long e: "mayl".
l3/milch|milk|A glass of milk, please.|Singular only. lch: an "l" followed by a soft "h" sound.
l3/zucker|sugar|We need sugar.|Singular only. z = ts: "tsoo-ka".
l3/pfannkuchen|pancake|We're making pancakes.|pf = p and f said together. ch after u is throaty.
l3/schokolade|chocolate|This is chocolate.|Singular only. Stress the second-to-last syllable: scho-ko-LA-de.
l3/brauchen|to need|We need flour.|ch after au is throaty. Followed directly by a noun: Ich brauche Eier.
l3/kaufen|to buy|I'm buying bananas.|
l3/hunger|hunger|I'm hungry!|Ich habe Hunger = I'm hungry (literally: I have hunger). Singular only.
l3/dann|then|I'm buying eggs and then flour.|
l3/helfen|to help|Can I help you?|e changes to i: du hilfst, er/sie hilft. Used with dir / Ihnen.
l3/ein|a, an (indefinite article)|That is an apple.|ein + der/das words · eine + die words. Plural: no article.
l3/kein|no, not a (negates nouns)|That's not an apple.|kein + der/das words · keine + die words and plural.
l3/apfel|apple|I'm buying a kilo of apples.|pf said together. The plural has ä: Äpfel.
l3/orange|orange|That is an orange.|The ending -ge is said "-zheh" as in French: o-RAN-zheh.
l3/kuchen|cake|The cake is great!|ch after u is throaty: "koo-khen". The plural doesn't change.
l3/kaffee|coffee|Do we have coffee?|
l3/saft|juice|A glass of juice, please.|The plural has ä: Säfte.
l3/broetchen|bread roll|I'm eating a bread roll.|-chen = small and always das (Brot → Brötchen).
l3/wuerstchen|small sausage, frankfurter|That's a little sausage.|-chen = small: die Wurst → das Würstchen.
l3/birne|pear|That's not a pear.|
l3/tomate|tomato|I'm buying three tomatoes.|
l3/was-ist-das|What is this/that?||
l3/wie-heisst-das|What is this called in German?||The most useful phrase for self-study: point at something and ask.
l3/das-ist-doch-kein|That's not a … at all!|That's not an egg!|doch adds surprise or contradiction.
l3/brot|bread, loaf|I'm buying a loaf of bread.|Long o; plural Brote.
l3/kartoffel|potato|I'm buying a kilo of potatoes.|Stress the second syllable.
l3/joghurt|yoghurt|I like eating yoghurt.|das Joghurt is also possible. j = y: "yo-gurt".
l3/zwiebel|onion|I need two onions.|zw = "tsv", ie = long ee.
l3/fisch|fish|I'm buying two fish.|sch = "sh".
l3/regal|shelf, shelves|There are apples on the shelf.|
l3/kaese|cheese|Do we have cheese?|Singular only. Long ä sounds like "ay": "kay-zeh".
l3/salz|salt|Do you have salt?|Singular only. z = ts.
l3/tee|tea|Do we have tea?|ee = long "ay": "tay".
l3/obst|fruit (in general)|I'm buying fruit.|Singular only: Obst = apples, pears, bananas… in general.
l3/gemuese|vegetables (in general)|I need vegetables.|Stress the second syllable.
l3/mineralwasser|mineral water|Do we need mineral water?|Singular only.
l3/wasser|water|A glass of water, please.|w = v: "vassa". Singular only.
l3/fleisch|meat|Do we have meat?|Singular only. ei = "eye", sch = "sh".
l3/reis|rice|Do you need rice?|Singular only. ei = "eye": "rice".
l3/wein|wine|Do we have wine?|w = v, ei = eye: "vine". Don't confuse Wein with Wien (Vienna).
l3/bier|beer|Do we have beer?|
l3/haben-wir|Do we have …?||Yes/no question: the verb comes first.
l3/haben-sie|Do you have …? (asking a shop assistant)|Do you have eggs?|
l3/ich-brauche|I need …|I need milk.|
l3/ja-natuerlich|Yes, of course.||
l3/hier-bitte|Here you are.||
l3/sonst-noch-etwas|Anything else?||
l3/nein-tut-mir-leid|No, I'm sorry.||
l3/n30|30 · thirty||Written with ß: dreißig (not dreizig). Say "dry-sikh".
l3/n40|40 · forty||
l3/n50|50 · fifty||
l3/n60|60 · sixty||Drop the s: sechzig (not sechszig).
l3/n70|70 · seventy||Drop -en: siebzig (not siebenzig).
l3/n80|80 · eighty||
l3/n90|90 · ninety||
l3/n100|100 · one hundred||einhundert is also possible.
l3/preis|price|The price is great!|ei = "eye": "price".
l3/cent|cent (1/100 euro)|That costs twenty cents.|Said "sent" as in English. No plural after a number: zwanzig Cent.
l3/euro|euro|That costs two euros.|eu = "oy": "oy-ro". No plural after a number: zwei Euro.
l3/prospekt|brochure, leaflet||
l3/sonderangebot|special offer||Sonder- = special + Angebot = offer.
l3/lebensmittel|food, groceries||Usually plural: die Lebensmittel.
l3/abteilung|department, section (in a shop)||
l3/wurst|sausage, cold cuts|A hundred grams of sausage, please.|The plural has ü: Würste.
l3/hackfleisch|minced meat||Singular only.
l3/oel|oil (cooking)||Long ö: round your lips and say "ay".
l3/wie-viel|how much|How much is that?|With countable plurals use wie viele: Wie viele Eier brauchen Sie?
l3/kosten|to cost|A loaf costs two euros.|Singular: kostet · plural: kosten.
l3/kilo|kilo (kg)|I'm buying a kilo of oranges.|Short form kg. No plural after a number: zwei Kilo.
l3/gramm|gram (g)|A hundred grams of cheese, please.|Short form g. Say: hundert Gramm.
l3/pfund|pound (500 g)|A pound of bread, please.|ein Pfund = 500 grams. pf said together.
l3/liter|litre (l)|A litre of milk costs 89 cents.|No plural after a number: drei Liter.
l3/flasche|bottle|A bottle of juice, please.|
l3/dose|can, tin|A tin of tomatoes costs 79 cents.|
l3/packung|packet, pack|A packet of tea, please.|
l3/becher|pot, tub (yoghurt, cream)|A tub of cream costs 59 cents.|ch after e is soft.
l3/sahne|cream (for cooking)||Singular only. The h is silent.
l3/was-kostet|How much is …? (one item)|How much is a kilo of apples?|
l3/was-kosten|How much are …? (several items)|How much are a hundred grams of cheese?|
l3/das-macht|That comes to … altogether|That comes to four euros twenty-eight altogether.|What the cashier says at the till.
l3/restaurant|restaurant|We're eating at a restaurant.|Said the French way with a nasal ending: "res-to-RANG".
l3/mensa|university canteen||s before a vowel sounds like z: "men-za".
l3/essen|to eat|I like eating fish.|e changes to i with du and er/sie. ss signals a short vowel.
l3/trinken|to drink|I like drinking tea.|
l3/kochen|to cook|My mother likes cooking.|ch after o is throaty.
l3/steak|steak|I'm having steak with salad.|An English word, but st at the start is said "sht": "shtayk".
l3/salat|salad; lettuce|I like eating salad.|
l3/haehnchen|chicken (as food)|The chicken tastes great!|Long ä; -chen is said soft, "-khen".
l3/pommes|chips, French fries||Full form: Pommes frites. Usually just Pommes (say "pom").
l3/pizza|pizza||zz sounds like "ts": "pit-sa".
l3/cola|cola||das Cola is also used.
l3/suppe|soup||
l3/glas|glass||The plural has ä: Gläser. Ein Glas Wasser = a glass of water.
l3/durst|thirst|I'm thirsty!|Ich habe Durst = I'm thirsty. Singular only.
l3/getraenk|drink, beverage||
l3/lieblingsessen|favourite food|My favourite food is pizza.|Lieblings- + another word = "favourite": Lieblingsgetränk, Lieblingsfilm.
l3/schmecken|to taste (good)|That tastes very good!|Often with gut / lecker: Das schmeckt gut!
l3/lecker|tasty, delicious|The cake is delicious!|
l3/gern|gladly; to like (doing)|I like drinking tea.|Comes after the verb: Ich esse gern Fisch. Negative: nicht gern. Stronger: sehr gern.
l3/rezept|recipe||
l3/portion|portion, serving|The recipe is for four servings.|-tion is said "-tsyohn".
l3/fuer|for|A recipe for two servings.|ü: round your lips and say "ee".
l3/einfach|simple, easy|The recipe is simple.|
l3/was-isst-du-gern|What do you like to eat?||
l3/was-trinkst-du-gern|What do you like to drink?||
l3/mein-lieblingsessen-ist|My favourite food is …||
l3/sosse|sauce|Spaghetti with tomato sauce!|
l3/typisch|typical||
l3/ganz|quite, completely|The recipe is quite simple.|
l3/studieren|to study (at university)||st at the start is said "sht": "shtoo-DEE-ren".
l3/pfeffer|pepper||Singular only. pf said together.
l3/reichen|to be enough|That's enough for three days.|
l3/tag|day||A final g sounds like k: "tahk".
l3/teuer|expensive|That's not expensive.|eu = "oy": "toy-a".
l3/zum-beispiel|for example||Short form z. B.
l3/gross|big, large; tall||ß = s; long o.
l4/wohnung|flat, apartment|The flat is bright.|Long o, silent h: "voh-noong". Related to wohnen (to live) from Lesson 2.
l4/haus|house|The house is big.|au sounds like "ow". Plural Häuser: äu sounds like "oy".
l4/zimmer|room|The room is dark.|z = ts. The plural doesn't change. A German "3-Zimmer-Wohnung" has 3 living/bedrooms; kitchen, bathroom and hall usually aren't counted.
l4/wohnzimmer|living room|The living room is over there.|Compound: wohnen + Zimmer. The gender comes from the last word: das Zimmer → das Wohnzimmer.
l4/schlafzimmer|bedroom|The bedroom is small.|schlafen = to sleep. A compound with Zimmer, so always das.
l4/kinderzimmer|children's room|The children's room is here.|Kinder = children (plural of das Kind, Lesson 2).
l4/arbeitszimmer|study, home office|Is there a study here too?|Arbeit = work. A room for working or studying at home.
l4/kueche|kitchen|Where is the kitchen?|ch after ü is soft.
l4/bad|bathroom|The bathroom is small but bright.|Long a. Plural Bäder.
l4/toilette|toilet|Where is the toilet, please?|Stress the middle: twa-LET-teh. In Germany the toilet is often a separate room from the bathroom.
l4/flur|hall, corridor (in a flat)|This is the hall.|Long u; a final r is very soft.
l4/balkon|balcony|The balcony is big.|Stress the last syllable: "bal-KONG".
l4/lampe|lamp|The lamp is old.|
l4/neu|new|My flat is new.|eu sounds like "oy": "noy". Opposite: alt (old).
l4/klein|small, little|The room is small.|ei sounds like "eye". Opposite: groß (big).
l4/hell|bright, light; light (colour)|The living room is bright.|ll signals a short e. Opposite: dunkel.
l4/dunkel|dark; dark (colour)|The bedroom is dark.|Opposite: hell.
l4/billig|cheap|The room is cheap.|A final -ig sounds like "-ikh": "bil-likh". Opposite: teuer (expensive).
l4/schoen|beautiful, nice|The kitchen is beautiful.|ö: lips rounded as for "o", tongue as for "ay". Opposite: hässlich.
l4/haesslich|ugly|The lamp is ugly.|ss signals a short vowel; -lich sounds like "-likh".
l4/dort|there, over there|The toilet is over there.|hier = here (near me); dort = there (away from me). Answers the question Wo?
l4/sag-mal|Tell me, … / Say, … (opening a question; Sag mal = informal, Sagen Sie mal = polite)||
l4/wo-ist-denn|So where's the kitchen? (denn makes the question sound friendlier)||
l4/das-ist-meine|This is my flat.||
l4/breit|wide, broad|The street is wide.|ei sounds like "eye". Opposite: schmal. breit is about width (roads, corridors, tables); groß is about size in general.
l4/schmal|narrow|The hall is narrow.|schm- sounds like "shm". Opposite: breit.
l4/modern|modern|The kitchen is very modern.|Stress the last syllable.
l4/richtig|right, correct|Yes, that's right.|A final -ig sounds like "-ikh". Opposite: falsch (Lesson 2).
l4/monat|month|The room costs 350 euros a month.|im Monat = per month.
l4/beispiel|example|For example: the bathroom is small.|zum Beispiel (z. B.) = for example. sp after Bei- sounds like "shp": "by-shpeel".
l4/kostet-im-monat|The room costs 350 euros a month.||
l4/wohnwagen|caravan, camper||
l4/schloss|castle, palace||Also "lock". Plural Schlösser.
l4/hochhaus|high-rise, tower block||hoch = high + Haus.
l4/huette|hut, cabin||
l4/hausboot|houseboat||
l4/villa|villa||
l4/tisch|table|The table is very big.|sch = "sh", short i.
l4/stuhl|chair|There are four chairs here.|st at the start sounds like "sht"; silent h, long u. Plural Stühle.
l4/bett|bed|The bed is very big.|tt signals a short e: "bet".
l4/sofa|sofa|The sofa is very nice.|s before a vowel sounds like z: "zoh-fa". The plural adds -s.
l4/sessel|armchair|The armchair is modern.|Ending -el: the plural doesn't change (die Sessel).
l4/schrank|cupboard, wardrobe|The wardrobe is old.|Any standing cupboard (wardrobe, kitchen cabinet…). Plural Schränke.
l4/teppich|carpet, rug|The carpet is ugly.|pp signals a short e; a final -ich sounds like "-ikh".
l4/moebel|furniture (plural)|The furniture is new.|Plural only.
l4/fernseher|television (set)|The TV is big.|A final -er sounds soft like "a". The plural doesn't change.
l4/kuehlschrank|fridge|The fridge is new.|kühl = cool + Schrank = cupboard.
l4/herd|cooker, stove|The cooker is old.|Long e; a final d sounds like t: "hairt".
l4/waschmaschine|washing machine|The washing machine is new.|waschen = to wash. -ine sounds like "-ee-neh".
l4/geraet|appliance, device|The cooker is an electrical appliance.|Elektrogeräte = electrical appliances (fridge, TV, cooker…).
